Transfer cell values to polygons with explicit area weights

Source: R/pg_area_weight.R
pg_area_weight.Rd

Extensive values are allocated by the share of each source cell overlapping a target and then summed. Intensive values are averaged with allocation area as the weight. Coverage columns report the share of relevant weight represented by non-missing observations.

Usage

pg_area_weight(
  data,
  crosswalk,
  values,
  target_id,
  variable_type,
  pgid = "pgid",
  time = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  na_rm = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing cell-level values.

crosswalk

A crosswalk created by pg_crosswalk().

values

Names of numeric value columns.

target_id

Name of the target identifier column in crosswalk.

variable_type

"extensive" or "intensive". Supply one value for all variables or a named vector with one type per value.

pgid

Name of the cell-ID column in data.

time

Optional temporal key column.

group

Optional additional grouping columns.

na_rm

Should missing source values be ignored?

Value

A data frame with target keys, transferred values, and a <value>_coverage diagnostic for every value.

Examples

crosswalk <- data.frame(
  pgid = c(1L, 2L), region = "a",
  overlap_area_km2 = c(1, 1), cell_fraction = c(1, 0.5),
  target_fraction = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
x <- data.frame(pgid = 1:2, population = c(10, 20))
pg_area_weight(x, crosswalk, "population", "region", "extensive")
#>   region population population_coverage
#> 1      a         20                   1
